subject: E2E latency targets & decision checklist — hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@veridian.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: latency targets and what we need next

Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the minimum artifacts we need to size a realistic hosted POC versus what you see from your incumbent: 

Summary from call:
- Veridian target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 340ms end-to-end for 95% of interactive traffic (human-facing triage flows).
- Peak concurrency: ~450 concurrent open streaming connections during peak daytime shifts (UTC-7).
- Typical prompt size: median 120 tokens input + median 80 tokens output. 99th-token-length bursts up to 1,200 tokens.
- Acceptable trade: can tolerate up to 2x cost for guaranteed p95 under 120ms, but p99 must be under 400ms or we trigger escalation.

What we asked for on the call (what would unblock a hosted SLO proposal):
1) 72-hr sample traffic (anonymized) with timestamps, request/response deltas, and any client-side queuing markers — CSV is fine (filename suggested).
2) Current provider SLA PDFs and any published latency percentiles for identical routes.
3) Confirmation of streaming requirements: are all 450 concurrent connections bi-directional streaming, or a mix of streaming + short polling?
4) Any hard cutover windows / blackout periods for testing (Ops constraints).

I've attached a one-page checklist + what we'll benchmark for the POC. If you can drop the CSV and the incumbent SLA by Friday 9/18 we'll schedule the POC run for the following week.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments referenced: veridian-latency-sample-traffic.csv (sample format), redwood-hosted-vs-incumbent-checklist.pdf
From: Sam Park <sam.park@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: latency targets and what we need next

Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications and what I uploaded to the shared Drive: 

Clarifications:
- The 450 concurrent figure is for live triage agents only; roughly 320 of those are long-lived streaming sessions (server -> client partials), the remainder are short polling / fetches. We can provide a breakout.
- Current provider published numbers (attached): p95 = 135ms, p99 = 520ms (these are their reported server-side numbers; end-to-end including our gateway averages +25ms).
- Blackout windows: our ops team requests no disruptive testing during Mon-Fri 08:00-10:00 PT due to scheduled backups; weekend testing preferred where possible.

I've uploaded: veridian-sample-traffic-202609.zip (contains anonymized CSV), and incumbent-SLA.pdf to the folder you shared. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abcd1234

Next step: can your SE run a lightweight traffic replay with our 24-hr sample and return a small table of p50/p95/p99 for the same request set? If so, propose we schedule a 2-hour slot next Wed (9/23) PST.

—Sam
Sam Park | Director of Platform Engineering, Veridian Health
sam.park@veridian.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: latency targets and what we need next

Thanks, Sam — copied the shortlist of what I'll need to prepare the replay and initial sizing. Putting this here so everything is explicit: 

Checklist for replay & hosted sizing
- Confirmed CSV fields: request_id, timestamp_client_send, timestamp_server_receive, request_tokens, response_tokens, streaming_flag (true/false), client_region, route_id. If you don't have all fields, include what you can and note gaps.
- Confirm which routes are latency-sensitive (agent-triage vs batch summaries). Mark route_id(s) to prioritize.
- Any per-customer routing that causes warm/cold model differences (e.g., dedicated model variants) — call that out.
- Auth pattern: are requests authenticated with a short-lived token, or behind a gateway token? We need to replicate auth handshake overhead if applicable.
- Max observed burst: please include the highest 1-minute concurrency snapshot (timestamp + concurrency).

What Redwood will report back after replay (deliverables)
- Replay p50/p95/p99 end-to-end numbers (hosted config) using identical request ordering and timing where possible.
- Streaming tail measurements (time to first partial, time to final token) per streaming session.
- Concurrency sensitivity: how p95/p99 shift as we throttle concurrency by 25%, 50% and 100% of observed peak.
- Suggested hosted config + expected unit cost delta vs incumbent (order-of-magnitude).

Scheduling: Ben — I can run the replay in the 2-hour slot on Wed 09/23. I need the anonymized 24-hr CSV by EOD Monday to validate the data. Sam, if you can confirm the CSV field mapping to the checklist above I'll prep the test harness.

Cheers,
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@veridian.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: latency targets and what we need next

Sam — perfect, thanks for the uploads and the detail. Quick operational notes and our proposed decision checklist before a formal POC kickoff: 

Operational asks before POC kickoff:
- Drop the 24-hr anonymized CSV into the shared folder (we saw the zip but need the CSV variant).
- Confirm which three routes we should prioritize for the POC (please flag agent-triage X, agent-lookup Y, and summary Z if those are the right names).
- Agree on the scheduled 2-hour window: Wed 2026-09-23 08:00-10:00 PT (Priyom reserved). Note the blackout constraints you mentioned; this slot is outside the backup window.

Decision checklist post-replay (what Veridian and Redwood agree to evaluate):
- Does hosted p95 meet <=120ms for prioritized routes?
- Does hosted p99 reduce to <=400ms with proposed config and acceptable cost?
- Do streaming-first-partial latencies match incumbent within 10%?
- Any client-side changes required (keepalive settings, token handoff)? Minimal or none preferred.

If we meet the checklist items, we will propose a 4-week pilot with a canary routing 10% of production traffic (with automatic fallback). If not, we'll iterate on batching/quantization/concurrency knobs and rerun benchmarks.

Action items (owners):
- Sam: drop CSV + confirm routes (owner: Sam) — due EOD Monday 09/20.
- Priyom: prepare replay harness + baseline report — will deliver by EOD Thu 09/24.
- Ben: schedule POC paperwork & DevOps contact — will send kickoff invite by Friday.

Thanks — looking forward to the replay.

Best,
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
